settings.heading: From Réunion
settings.body:
Réunion is a volcanic island in the Indian Ocean, French since the 1600s and Creole in its kitchen. Sweet potato is a common ingredient, and gâteau patate (sweet potato cake) is a staple Sunday bake for many families.

Our recipe is a family recipe. It was written for a family, not a bakery: steamed sweet potato, eggs, vanilla, a little flour, baked long and slow.

settings.heading: Built to travel
settings.body:
We changed two things. We roast the sweet potatoes whole so the sugars concentrate and the crumb holds together, and we bake each cake small enough to fit a jersey pocket or a vest.

What did not change: no shortcuts, no preservatives, the same vanilla these islands have grown for generations. A cake keeps ten days at room temperature and takes heat, cold and a full day of bouncing without falling apart.

settings.heading: La Diagonale des Fous
settings.body:
La Diagonale des Fous — the Madmen's Diagonal — runs roughly 165 km across Réunion, coast to coast over the volcano, with about 9,500 metres of climbing. It is the island's race.

Cakes from this recipe have been carried at aid stations along the route. Thirty hours in, when gels stop working, a slice of something a runner grew up eating still goes down. That is the whole idea.

settings.title: A Réunion recipe, made for athletes and adventures.
settings.standfirst: Sweet potato cake —gâteau patate in French— is an everyday dessert on Réunion Island. This is one family's version, baked for adventures.
settings.quote: Made on the island, for the parts of the island without roads.
